subject: math
cluster: Draw informal comparative inferences about two populations
intro: To compare two data distributions that have similar spreads, express the difference between their centers as a multiple of one measure of variability. Subtract the two centers, then divide by the variability (MAD or IQR). A small multiple means the distributions overlap a lot; a large multiple means they are clearly separated.

items.prompt: Team A has a mean of $12$ points and Team B has a mean of $18$ points. Both teams have a mean absolute deviation (MAD) of $3$ points. The difference between the means is how many times the MAD?

steps: Find the difference between the centers: $|18 - 12| = 6$.
Divide the difference by the MAD: $\frac{6}{3} = 2$.
The means differ by $2$ times the MAD.

items.prompt: Class 1 has a mean test score of $70$ and Class 2 has a mean test score of $80$. Both classes have a MAD of $5$ points. Express the difference between the means as a multiple of the MAD.

steps: The means differ by $2$ times the MAD.

items.prompt: Garden X has a mean plant height of $20$ cm and Garden Y has a mean plant height of $26$ cm. Both gardens have a MAD of $2$ cm. The difference between the means is how many times the MAD?

steps: The means differ by $3$ times the MAD.

items.prompt: Brand A batteries last a mean of $30$ hours and Brand B batteries last a mean of $34$ hours. Both brands have a MAD of $4$ hours. Express the difference between the means as a multiple of the MAD.

steps: The means differ by $1$ time the MAD.

items.prompt: Route 1 has a median travel time of $40$ minutes and Route 2 has a median travel time of $55$ minutes. Both routes have an interquartile range (IQR) of $5$ minutes. The difference between the medians is how many times the IQR?

steps: The medians differ by $3$ times the IQR.

items.prompt: Store A has a median wait time of $8$ minutes and Store B has a median wait time of $14$ minutes. Both stores have an IQR of $3$ minutes. Express the difference between the medians as a multiple of the IQR.

steps: The medians differ by $2$ times the IQR.

items.prompt: Group 1 has a mean of $50$ and Group 2 has a mean of $50$. Both groups have a MAD of $6$. The difference between the means is how many times the MAD?

steps: The means differ by $0$ times the MAD, so the centers are the same.

items.prompt: Player A scores a mean of $15$ points and Player B scores a mean of $24$ points. Both players have a MAD of $3$ points. Express the difference between the means as a multiple of the MAD.

steps: The means differ by $3$ times the MAD.

items.prompt: Pond A has a mean fish length of $10$ cm and Pond B has a mean fish length of $18$ cm. Both ponds have a MAD of $4$ cm. The difference between the means is how many times the MAD?

steps: The means differ by $2$ times the MAD.

items.prompt: Section 1 has a median quiz score of $7$ and Section 2 has a median quiz score of $9$. Both sections have an IQR of $2$ points. Express the difference between the medians as a multiple of the IQR.

steps: The medians differ by $1$ time the IQR.

items.prompt: Two seventh-grade classes recorded their heights. The difference between the two mean heights is $3$ times the MAD. Does this multiple show that the distributions overlap a lot or are clearly separated? Answer overlap a lot or clearly separated.

steps: A large multiple of the MAD means the centers are far apart compared with the spread.
Since the difference is $3$ MADs, that is a large multiple.
The two distributions are clearly separated, not heavily overlapping.

items.prompt: The difference between the centers of two distributions is $0$ times the MAD. Does this multiple show that the distributions overlap a lot or are clearly separated? Answer overlap a lot or clearly separated.

steps: A multiple of $0$ means the two centers are at the same value.
When the centers are equal and the spreads are similar, the distributions sit on top of each other.
The two distributions overlap a lot.

items.prompt: Bakery A sells a mean of $40$ loaves per day and Bakery B sells a mean of $52$ loaves per day. Both bakeries have a MAD of $4$ loaves. Express the difference between the means as a multiple of the MAD.

steps: The means differ by $3$ times the MAD.

items.prompt: City A has a median rainfall of $6$ cm and City B has a median rainfall of $12$ cm. Both cities have an IQR of $6$ cm. The difference between the medians is how many times the IQR?

steps: The medians differ by $1$ time the IQR.

items.prompt: Phone A has a mean download speed of $25$ and Phone B has a mean download speed of $35$. Both phones have a MAD of $5$. Express the difference between the means as a multiple of the MAD.

steps: The means differ by $2$ times the MAD.
